# Queryable

A schema is _Queryable_ when it can find its data in the store from args alone, without a response.
[Normalization](https://dataclient.io/vue/concepts/normalization) makes this possible: it stores each Entity once, by its primary key, no matter
which response delivered it.

Queryability allows for higher performance navigation. Data that one request loaded renders on every page that asks
for it. A detail page opened from a list renders at once, and makes no request while that data is fresh.

Open a post below. `PostDetail` renders without a loading state, because the list already stored that `Post`.

Files with a `route` are pages mounted at that path, with its params as props (vue-router `props: true`).

```ts title="Resources"
import { Entity, resource } from '@data-client/rest';

export class User extends Entity {
  id = 0;
  name = '';
  username = '';
  email = '';
  phone = '';
  website = '';

  get profileImage() {
    return `https://i.pravatar.cc/64?img=${this.id + 4}`;
  }

  static key = 'User';
}
export const UserResource = resource({
  urlPrefix: 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com',
  path: '/users/:id',
  schema: User,
});

export class Post extends Entity {
  id = 0;
  author = User.fromJS();
  title = '';
  body = '';

  static key = 'Post';

  static schema = {
    author: User,
  };
}
export const PostResource = resource({
  path: '/posts/:id',
  schema: Post,
  paginationField: 'page',
});
```

```html title="PostDetail.vue" route="/posts/:id" {6}
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useSuspense } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { PostResource } from './Resources';

  const props = defineProps<{ id: string }>();
  const post = await useSuspense(PostResource.get, () => ({ id: props.id }));
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <header>
      <div class="listItem spaced">
        <div class="author">
          <Avatar :src="post.author.profileImage" />
          <small>{{ post.author.name }}</small>
        </div>
        <h4>{{ post.title }}</h4>
      </div>
    </header>
    <p>{{ post.body }}</p>
  </div>
</template>
```

  defineProps<{ post: Post }>();
</script>

<template>
  <div class="listItem spaced">
    <Avatar :src="post.author.profileImage" />
    <div>
      <h4>
        <RouterLink :to="`/posts/${post.id}`">{{ post.title }}</RouterLink>

```html title="PostList.vue" route="/" {7}
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useSuspense } from '@data-client/vue';
  import LoadMore from './LoadMore.vue';
  import PostItem from './PostItem.vue';
  import { PostResource } from './Resources';

  const posts = await useSuspense(PostResource.getList);
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <PostItem v-for="post in posts" :key="post.pk()" :post="post" />
    <LoadMore />
  </div>
</template>
```

```html title="LoadMore.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { computed } from 'vue';
  import { useController, useLoading, useQuery } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { PostResource } from './Resources';

  const ctrl = useController();
  const posts = useQuery(PostResource.getList.schema);
  const [nextPage, isPending] = useLoading(() =>
    ctrl.fetch(PostResource.getList.getPage, { page: 2 }),
  );
  const canLoadMore = computed(
    () => !!posts.value && posts.value.length % 3 === 0,
  );
</script>

<template>
  <div v-if="canLoadMore" class="loadMore">
    <button @click="nextPage">
      {{ isPending ? '...' : 'Load more' }}
    </button>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Querying the store {#query}

A Queryable schema has a [queryKey(args)](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/schema#queryable) method. It returns what a response would have
normalized to, and returns it only for data the store holds.

[useQuery()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/useQuery) asks this question directly. `useQuery(Post, { id })` returns the stored `Post`, or
`undefined` when the store doesn't hold it. It never fetches.

Each schema answers in its own way:

- An [Entity](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity) returns its primary key. By default, args with the fields `pk()` reads, like `{ id }`,
  find it. `pk()`, [indexes](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#indexes) or `queryKey` itself change which args do
  ([Queryable by args](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#pk-args)).
- An object schema like `{ data: Post }` combines its members' results.
- [Collection](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Collection), [All](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/All), [Union](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Union), [Query](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Query) and
  [Scalar](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Scalar) are Queryable too ([what each returns](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/schema#queryable)).
- [Array](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Array) and [Values](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Values) are not. Use a [Collection](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Collection) or
  [All](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/All) for a list that should be Queryable.

## Endpoints query before they fetch {#endpoints}

An endpoint with a Queryable schema asks the same question before it fetches. Reading an endpoint uses the first of
these that applies:

1. The endpoint has a response of its own. It reads that response, with that response's expiry.
2. The endpoint's schema is Queryable, and the store's result for its args is complete: no part of it is `undefined`.
   It reads that result.
3. Otherwise the data is missing, so the endpoint fetches.

So what `useQuery()` can find, an endpoint doesn't wait to fetch. When `useQuery(Post, { id })` returns a post,
`useSuspense(PostResource.get, { id })` renders it without waiting for a fetch. The exceptions are an endpoint that
was invalidated, or one that is invalidIfStale and stale ([expiry](#expiry)).

The two differ in what they do with the answer:

|                               | [useQuery(schema, ...args)](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/useQuery) | Reading an endpoint with that schema         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Queries the store             | Always                                                              | Until the endpoint has a response of its own |
| Part of the result is missing | Returns `undefined`; an object schema returns the object without it | Fetches                                      |
| [Expiry](#expiry)             | Ignored                                                             | Applies                                      |
| Fetches                       | Never                                                               | When data is missing or stale                |

This applies wherever an endpoint is read: [useSuspense()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/useSuspense), [useDLE()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/useDLE),
[useCache()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/useCache), [useLive()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/useLive), [useFetch()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/useFetch),
[Controller.getResponse()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/Controller#getResponse) and
[Controller.fetchIfStale()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/Controller#fetchIfStale). [Controller.fetch()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/Controller#fetch) always
requests.

### Stored data keeps its expiry {#expiry}

A complete result is treated like a response. It expires when the earliest-expiring Entity in it does, and the
[expiry policy](./expiry-policy.vue.md) applies as usual:

- While the result is fresh, the endpoint makes no request.
- Once it is stale, it still renders, and the endpoint refetches.
- An [invalidIfStale](./expiry-policy.vue.md#endpointinvalidifstale) endpoint treats a stale result as
  [Invalid](./expiry-policy.vue.md#expiry-status), and an [invalidated](./expiry-policy.vue.md#invalidate) endpoint treats any
  result that way, so they wait for a fetch.
- An Entity that fails [validate()](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#validate) counts as missing.

### Which results are complete {#complete}

- An Entity stored by any response is found by every endpoint whose schema holds that Entity and whose args produce its
  `pk`.
- Args `queryKey` doesn't read, like `expand` in `{ id, expand: 'comments' }`, don't affect the result.
- An object schema like `{ data: Post }` is complete when every member is. An Array member never is. A Collection
  member is when the store holds it for those args. Two Entities must both be found by the same args.
- Until the endpoint's own response arrives, the result holds only what the schema declares. Plain values in it, like
  `total: 0`, are returned as written. Response fields it leaves out, like a `meta`, are `undefined`.

### Fields are not checked {#fields}

Finding an Entity doesn't check which fields it has. When list items lack fields the detail page shows, the detail
renders those fields' defaults, and doesn't fetch while the list data is fresh. To make it fetch, give the list a
summary Entity and make the detail Entity require the rest with [validate()](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#validate)
([Partial entities](https://dataclient.io/rest/guides/partial-entities)).

## After mutations {#mutations}

A mutation's response is stored the way any response is. Reads that come after it find the result in the store, so
the next page renders at once and makes no request.

The app below sends one `GET`, for its `Team` page. Every page after that renders from the store, and only the
mutations send requests.

Files with a `route` are pages mounted at that path, with its params as props (vue-router `props: true`).

```ts title="Resources" {32-34}
import { Collection, Entity, resource } from '@data-client/rest';

export class Todo extends Entity {
  id = 0;
  userId = 0;
  title = '';
  completed = false;

  static key = 'Todo';
}
export const TodoResource = resource({
  urlPrefix: 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com',
  path: '/todos/:id',
  searchParams: {} as { userId?: string | number } | undefined,
  schema: Todo,
  optimistic: true,
});

export class User extends Entity {
  id = 0;
  name = '';
  todos: Todo[] = [];

  get profileImage() {
    return `https://i.pravatar.cc/64?img=${this.id + 4}`;
  }

  static key = 'User';

  static schema = {
    // the list TodoResource.getList({ userId }) reads
    todos: new Collection([Todo], {
      nestKey: parent => ({ userId: parent.id }),
    }),
  };
}
export const UserResource = resource({
  urlPrefix: 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com',
  path: '/users/:id',
  schema: User,
});
```

```html title="Team.vue" route="/"
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useSuspense } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { UserResource } from './Resources';

  const users = await useSuspense(UserResource.getList);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="list">
    <div v-for="user in users" :key="user.pk()" class="listItem">
      <Avatar :src="user.profileImage" />
      <RouterLink :to="`/users/${user.id}`">{{ user.name }}</RouterLink>
      <span class="meta">
        {{ user.todos.filter(todo => !todo.completed).length }} open
      </span>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

```html title="UserPage.vue" route="/users/:id" {12-13}
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useFetch, useSuspense } from '@data-client/vue';
  import NewTodo from './NewTodo.vue';
  import { TodoResource, UserResource } from './Resources';
  import TodoItem from './TodoItem.vue';

  const props = defineProps<{ id: string }>();
  const userArgs = () => ({ id: props.id });
  const todoArgs = () => ({ userId: props.id });
  // start the second read before awaiting the first
  useFetch(TodoResource.getList, todoArgs);
  const user = await useSuspense(UserResource.get, userArgs);
  const todos = await useSuspense(TodoResource.getList, todoArgs);
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <h2>{{ user.name }}</h2>
    <div class="list">
      <TodoItem v-for="todo in todos" :key="todo.pk()" :todo="todo" />
      <NewTodo :userId="user.id" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

```html title="TodoItem.vue" {9-13,15}
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useController } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { TodoResource, type Todo } from './Resources';

  const props = defineProps<{ todo: Todo }>();
  const ctrl = useController();

  const handleChange = (e: Event) =>
    ctrl.fetch(
      TodoResource.partialUpdate,
      { id: props.todo.id },
      { completed: (e.target as HTMLInputElement).checked },
    );
  const handleDelete = () =>
    ctrl.fetch(TodoResource.delete, { id: props.todo.id });
</script>

<template>
  <div class="listItem nogap">
    <label>
      <input
        type="checkbox"
        :checked="todo.completed"
        @change="handleChange"
      />
      <RouterLink :to="`/todos/${todo.id}`">{{ todo.title }}</RouterLink>
    </label>
    <CancelButton @click="handleDelete" />
  </div>
</template>
```

```html title="NewTodo.vue" {11-14}
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useController } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { TodoResource } from './Resources';

  const props = defineProps<{ userId: number }>();
  const ctrl = useController();

  const handleKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === 'Enter') {
      const input = e.target as HTMLInputElement;
      ctrl.fetch(TodoResource.getList.push, {
        userId: props.userId,
        title: input.value,
      });
      input.value = '';
    }
  };
</script>

<template>
  <div class="listItem nogap">
    <label>
      <input type="checkbox" name="new" :checked="false" disabled />
      <input
        type="text"
        aria-label="New todo"
        placeholder="New todo"
        @keydown="handleKeyDown"
      />
    </label>
  </div>
</template>
```

```html title="TodoPage.vue" route="/todos/:id" {9,14-18}
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useController, useFetch, useSuspense } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { TodoResource, UserResource } from './Resources';

  const props = defineProps<{ id: string }>();
  const ctrl = useController();
  // start the second read before awaiting the first
  useFetch(UserResource.getList);
  const todo = await useSuspense(TodoResource.get, () => ({ id: props.id }));
  const users = await useSuspense(UserResource.getList);

  // move, not partialUpdate: the todo changes lists
  const assign = (userId: number) =>
    ctrl.fetch(
      TodoResource.getList.move,
      { id: todo.value.id },
      { userId },
    );
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <h2>{{ todo.title }}</h2>
    <p class="meta">{{ todo.completed ? 'Done' : 'Open' }}</p>
    <section>
      <h3>Owner</h3>
      <div class="list">
        <button
          v-for="user in users"
          :key="user.pk()"
          class="listItem"
          :aria-current="user.id === todo.userId"
          @click="assign(user.id)"
        >
          <Avatar :src="user.profileImage" :size="24" />
          {{ user.name }}
        </button>
      </div>
    </section>
  </div>
</template>
```

- `UserPage` reads `TodoResource.getList({ userId })`, which was never fetched. `/users` nests each user's todos in a
  [Collection](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Collection). Its [nestKey](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Collection#nestKey) returns the same args, so
  `user.todos` and that list are one list in the store.
- `NewTodo` creates with [getList.push](./resource.vue.md#push). The todo joins every stored list its args match,
  and `TodoPage` renders it from the response.
- `TodoPage` changes the owner with [getList.move](./resource.vue.md#move). The todo leaves the old owner's list
  and joins the new owner's.

These reads keep their [expiry](#expiry). Data is stale after a minute by default: a page then still renders at once,
and refetches.

### What renders after each mutation {#mutation-reads}

| Mutation                                                                                                                                              | Renders next, without a fetch                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create: [getList.push](./resource.vue.md#push), [getList.unshift](./resource.vue.md#unshift)                                                                  | The new item's detail. Every stored list whose args match, and any [All](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/All) list |
| Edit: [update](./resource.vue.md#update), [partialUpdate](./resource.vue.md#partialupdate)                                                                    | The item's detail with the new values, even when nothing fetched that detail                                      |
| Edit that changes its list: [getList.move](./resource.vue.md#move)                                                                                        | The list it left and the list it joined                                                                           |
| Take out of a list: [getList.remove](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#remove)                                                                                        | The lists without it. Its detail still renders                                                                    |
| [delete](./resource.vue.md#delete)                                                                                                                        | The lists without it. Its detail is [Invalid](./expiry-policy.vue.md#expiry-status), so it fetches                    |
| No request, like a websocket [Manager](https://dataclient.io/vue/concepts/managers): [Controller.set()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/Controller#set) | The detail of an Entity it wrote, and the list of a Collection it wrote                                           |

### Lists are found by their args {#collection-args}

A [Collection](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Collection) stores one list for each set of args, like `{ userId: 1 }`. Reads and mutations
both find a list by those args, not by the endpoint that fetched it.

- Endpoints that share a Collection read the same list for the same args. `/users/:userId/todos` renders what
  `/todos?userId=` loaded when both use `TodoResource.getList.schema`.
- A Collection nested in an Entity takes its args from [nestKey](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Collection#nestKey), as `User.todos` does
  above.
- [argsKey](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Collection#argsKey) chooses which args name the list. Leave out args that don't filter it, like
  `expand`, and reads that differ only in those args share one list.
- `push` and `unshift` choose lists by the request's args and body, not by the response. Send the fields that lists
  filter by, like `userId`.
- `update` and `partialUpdate` change an item where it is. When an edit changes which list holds the item, use
  `move`.

## Other ways to query {#uses}

Every API that reads the store without an endpoint takes a Queryable schema and args:

- [Query](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Query) computes a sorted, filtered or aggregated view from another Queryable schema.
- [Controller.get()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/Controller#get) and [Snapshot.get()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/Snapshot#get) read the store in
  [Managers](https://dataclient.io/vue/concepts/managers), event handlers and
  [getOptimisticResponse](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#getoptimisticresponse).
- [Controller.set()](https://dataclient.io/vue/api/Controller#set) writes with the same schema and args.

[Queryable schemas](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/schema#queryable) lists every use.
